# A331940: addends k > 0 such that the polynomial x^2 + x + k produces a record of its Hardy-Littlewood constant.
# Columns: n, a(n) = k, and C, the Hardy-Littlewood constant of x^2 + x + a(n) (the C of the table in the entry's comments), rounded to 29 decimal places (30 significant digits).
# C(k) = 2 * Product over odd primes p of (1 - (D|p)/(p-1)), D = 1 - 4k; C = 0 for even k.
# Each C was computed to 34 significant digits by Cohen's method (L(1,chi) and L(j,chi) by the approximate functional equation, no class number used),
# and checked against a rigorous interval from the class number h(1-4k) (class number formula times an absolutely convergent Euler product);
# h(1-4k) was confirmed by an analytic computation, by counting sums of three squares, and by enumerating the reduced forms.
# The rounding to 29 decimals holds for every row over the full error bound of the 34-digit value.
# a(1)..a(11) and their C to 5 decimals are in the entry's own table; this file covers n = 12..34.
